character.lede: A dark-timber box with a floating two-band lid stands beside a white double-gable wing, with a French entry on a tiled porch. A timber deck wrapped by a reflecting rill and a koi fountain fill the garden.

spots.line: A chesterfield sofa and two club chairs face a round table.
A chaise, a rattan chair and a potting bench share the garden room.
A house bed, a small desk and a beanbag fill Lea's room.

facts.style: Two-storey modern: a dark-timber flat-roofed box under a floating two-band lid, white and striped piers, a French entry on a tiled porch and a glazed bay with slat fins, stands forward of a white double-gable wing whose front gable is an open frame; gravel forecourt, a timber deck wrapped by a reflecting rill, a koi fountain by the drive

character.truths: The Core sits on a console in the Library Lounge, in sight of the door. There is no television. The kitchen has an island. Timber deck, reflecting rill, koi fountain, pool.

details.rule: every beat of an adult or teen persona (13 or older) gets a detail (before, after, steps, fact); pair beats first

paperless: [note] AI features are off by default. If you turn them on they can use a local model.
[note] Office document conversion is not wired up in this build; OCR and archiving of PDFs and scans works.
forgejo: [note] Gitea does the same job. Name one Git host per household, not both.
[note] The listing mentions Forgejo Actions CI. The package ships the forge and its database only, no runner, so do not show a CI run.
[claims] Say where the repositories are (on the Core). Do not say it syncs with, or is compatible with, GitHub.
Listing says "fully self-hosted and private": over-claim, do not repeat.
Listing mentions Forgejo Actions CI, but no runner ships: never show a CI run.
koodo-reader: marketplace: Listing text says nothing is sent to a cloud service; the reader has outside-calling features (translation, lookup, speech).
ci-planning: [cloud-link] Two-way Google Calendar sync exists but is off by default and needs a Google OAuth client. Do not say it never touches Google.
[note] Local-model briefings, task extraction and auto-scheduling appear only when Ollama is reachable.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.

[cloud-link] Crash reports go to Companion Intelligence unless "Share crash reports" is turned off at install (it is on by default). Credentials, file paths, request bodies and memories are stripped first. Do not write t
Two way Google Calendar sync exists, off by default: never say it never touches Google.
firefly-iii: [cloud-link] Bank import through GoCardless or Spectre is an outside service. CSV import stays local.
[claims] Bookkeeping tool. No financial advice and no savings promises.
marketplace: Replaces lists Mint, which Intuit retired in 2024.
pi-hole: [claims] Network-wide blocking at DNS. Do not call it parental control or promise safety.
Blocks ad, tracker and bad domains at DNS: not parental control and no promise of safety
Unblocked lookups are forwarded to an upstream resolver (the upstream demo dashboard lists a public DNS, dns.google), so a DNS provider still sees them and it is not offline
Overlaps AdGuard Home: one per household
grocy: [note] The listing is short. Describe pantry stock, shopping lists, recipes and chores only.
Short listing: describe pantry stock, shopping lists, recipes, tasks and habits only (catalog)
Upstream demo screenshot shows a dollar total: prices on screen
jupyterlab: [note] One password set at install. The notebook kernel runs the code on the Core; installing a Python package reaches the internet.

[claims] Neither the manifest, the live store nor the Portal alternatives table (origin/main) names anything it replaces, so there is no replaces chip. The CI-Common campaign reference says MATLAB or RStudio, from a sour
QA screenshot is the token and password wall: reject.
Logo file shows only the orange arcs, not the Jupyter wordmark.
vikunja: QA shot is a sign-in wall
steam-headless: [cloud-link] Steam needs a Valve account to sign in, and the game library and the purchases are Valve's. The Core runs the session; the account stays with Valve. Say that, never "no account".

[hardware] The listing asks for GPU passthrough for best performance and the Hub package declares no GPU device, so a given Core may not run a given game well. Say what the Core does (it runs the session at home), never

[claims] No frame rate, resolution or latency figure, and not "smooth". Never "gaming PC", "console replacement" or "cloud gaming replacement" in the text. The chip may read "replaces GeForce Now" or "replaces Xbox Cloud

[note] It shows a streamed desktop with sound in a browser (noVNC), so the screen needs a browser, not a console. The container runs privileged with host access: do not call it sandboxed. Keep the stream on the home netw
[note] Persona decision 2026-10-15 (Liam Broza): re-admitted from the old cloud-account exclusion for the gamer archetype, with the caveats above.
blockbench: Projects live in the browser (IndexedDB) or in files the person saves: the Core serves the app, it does not hold the models
The listing names Minecraft models; say "game models" or "block models" in copy
Free-text store claim "never sees your models" is accurate for the container
obsidian: [licence] Obsidian is not open source. Do not call it open source.
[note] An Obsidian MCP entry exists so an agent can read and write the vault.
not open source (catalog: never say so)
listing says private and offline: do not repeat
notes are files on the Core, the app is streamed
project-nomad: [public-access] Ships without authentication. For trusted home networks only. Never describe it as exposed.
[note] amd64 only (fine on the Core). Internet is needed once for setup and downloads.
[claims] Educational content comes from third-party sources. Do not promise grades.
Ships without authentication: home network only, never described as exposed.
Needs the internet once for setup and downloads; never "fully offline" or "anywhere".
libretranslate: [note] Works offline once language models are downloaded.
Listing says "works fully offline": banned wording (sec-offline)
Likely already heavy in the existing stories
jotty: Public share links need outside reach
Everything is Markdown and JSON files, no database
wallos: [note] Fetches logos for popular services from outside.
opencode: [cloud-link] The Hub wires it to the Core's local model by default (hub_integration inference). The app can also connect to cloud providers with a key you add inside it; leave that off. A coding agent is private only on
[claims] Never claim parity with a hosted coding model and never a speed figure. The agent edits files, so the beat shows the person approving the change (agents prepare, people approve).
[note] The web interface has no sign-in unless a server password is set at install. The older OpenCode Web listing is superseded; name only OpenCode.
[note] Added 2026-10-15 for the builder archetype: the old cloud-or-developer exclusion lumped it with apps that need cloud keys; this one is wired to the local model.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
syncthing: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
audiomass: The Core only serves the page: decoded audio and edits live in the viewer's browser, so "sits on the Core" is false until the person saves a file where they choose
Short description says "audio never leaves the appliance": an absolute; paraphrase
joplin: [note] Joplin Server only; the Joplin apps are separate.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
marketplace: Joplin Server carries its own Personal Use License: not open source and limited for business use.
komga: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
booklore: [cloud-link] Fetches metadata and covers from outside.
airtrail: Logbook and statistics, not live flight tracking (listing short_desc says "flight tracking")
Does not claim live flight status; story must say logbook
librephotos: [note] First setup takes 5 to 10 minutes while models and migrations start.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
Face recognition is sensitive: say what it does, never that it "knows" people
Overlaps Immich; use it to relieve Immich's share
miniflux: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
Integrations push to outside services if switched on (Pocket, Telegram, webhooks)
librespeed: Say "the link to the Core" or "the Wi-Fi in this room"; never "internet speed"
No speed figures in copy (num rules): show the act, not a number
Listing says "privacy-focused" and "no tracking": do not repeat
